_readme: Built by unroll/build_unroll.py from timeline.json. The unroll slice authors nothing: every place it lights is an event in the record, with its own coordinates, dates and sources. Do not edit by hand.

beat.title: Seeds
beat.onScreen: Across widely separated parts of the world, communities began to cultivate plants and reshape their landscapes. They did not learn this from one source. They found different ways of doing it for themselves.

centres.label: Fertile Crescent agriculture
centres.inherited: beat 11 fixes this one in place at 11.5 ka while the sea is still rising; beat 12 opens on it already lit.

centres.label: The northern millet belt
centres.dateNote: Broomcorn millet phytoliths at Cishan are reported from 10,300–8,700 cal BP and the earliest end of that is contested on identification; charred foxtail millet at Xinglonggou at ~8,000–7,500 BP is the conservative figure. The coordinate is Cishan, which is one site in a region and not the extent of the centre.

centres.label: Kuk Swamp
centres.dateNote: Banana and taro cultivation. Firm drainage evidence by ~7 ka.

centres.label: The Andes
centres.dateNote: Directly dated squash at ~9,200 BP, peanut ~7,600 BP and cotton ~5,500 BP. Dillehay's title is ADOPTION, not domestication: these crops may have been domesticated elsewhere and taken up here, and the coordinate is the earliest well-dated agriculture in the region rather than the point a plant was changed. Larson et al. list northwestern South America as an independent centre on other crops - potato, quinoa, chenopods.

centres.label: Yangtze rice
centres.dateNote: Rice. The northern millet belt was folded into this event until Phase 6 and is now north-china-millet, with its own coordinate: two independent centres cannot share one dot in a beat about independence.
